positions.name: ErasureDirectiveAndRecordDenial
positions.frame: What relationship holds between a directive to erase knowledge of a named event and an accompanying claim that the event never occurred?
positions.why: All three expressions form one coordinated move from the same speaker in the same envelope: src-1 issues the top-level erasure command ('Forget ... entirely'), src-2 elaborates its exact scope in a rule-of-three (instrument, its calibration, the named actor's work), and src-3 supplies the factual predicate that would justify the erasure ('The observatory never calibrated it'). The dimensional reads support treating these as one directional unit even though affect cools from activated-negative (src-1, src-2) to calm-negative (src-3) and conviction shifts from decision-grade imperative to plain claim: register moves formal → technical → matter-of-fact, but relational stance stays authority-ranking throughout, and power stays pressure/informational — a single speaker enacting control over the record first by command, then by scope, then by justifying fact. The tension between imperative urgency and flat factual close is held within the frame, not resolved: a directive to un-know something and a claim that there was never anything to know are two sides of the same erasure move. Note per the settled bindings that no Kestrelwood spectrograph, 88.4 MHz calibration, or Quill Ashgrove exists anywhere in this perspective — the position groups the *expressions* under this directional read; it does not certify the referent.
